the development of a mathematical model that allows the analysis of thermoluminescent glow curves and their comparison with experimental data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thermoluminescence data obtained for photosystem II reaction centers of higher plants can be described in terms of the model proposed in the work, which includes the S states and tyrozine Z on the donor side and the primary and secondary quinine acceptors on the donor side.

the proposed approach allows us to determine the activation energies of forward electron transfer and backward reactions of electron and proton transfer in the reaction center of photosystem II and to describe experimental data on the thermoluminescence kinetics of higher plants in the temperature range from 77 to 250 K.
the model of thermoluminescent glow curves of photosystem II, proposed by us, is able to satisfactorily explain the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermoluminescence glow curve of photosystem II can be described in the frame of our model.
the experimental glow curves of photosynthetic organisms, obtained at the temperature range 77–200 K, are described by a model of thermoluminescent bands with a single activation energy.
the thermoluminescence model proposed is applicable to the analysis of thermoluminescent curves of photosystem II of higher plants.
